## Start here

### `create_artwork`

START HERE when the user asks you to make a picture from a prompt. Creates the document and either  
GENERATES it with an image model (realistic photos, cinematic stills, anything photographic) or sets it up  
for you to PAINT it with Krita's own brushes. approach: auto (decides: realism or a connected image model  
-> generate; hand-made / graphic requests or no model -> paint), generate, paint, or hybrid (generate,  
then add layers for you to paint over and refine). style: photo, cinematic, portrait, product, fashion,  
street, landscape, macro, food, architecture, drone, concept_art, illustration, anime, watercolor,  
oil_painting, 3d_render, pixel_art, comic, sketch (default: guessed from the prompt). aspect: 1:1, 4:3,  
3:4, 3:2, 2:3, 16:9, 9:16, 21:9, 4:5, 5:4 (or width/height). count = variations to compare (generate;  
default 4 on a local GPU, 1 on paid cloud services, which charge per image).  
For painting it returns a plan; then use brush_stroke / draw_shapes / add_svg, look with canvas_snapshot,  
and iterate. To turn your painted sketch into a realistic image later: generate_image(control=[{"layer":  
"Sketch", "type": "scribble"}], style="photo").

Parameters: `prompt`: str, `approach`: str = `'auto'`, `style`: Optional = `None`, `aspect`: str = `'1:1'`, `width`: Optional = `None`, `height`: Optional = `None`, `count`: Optional = `None`, `backend`: Optional = `None`, `model`: Optional = `None`, `seed`: Optional = `None`, `name`: Optional = `None`

## Documents

### `krita_status`

Krita version, the sandboxed workspace folder, and the open documents (index, size, active).

### `dismiss_recovery_dialog`

Krita asks at start-up whether to recover autosaved files after a crash, and nothing else can happen until  
someone answers. This cancels that question and keeps the autosaves (it neither recovers nor deletes them).  
Other dialogs are left alone. Use it when calls fail or hang right after Krita starts.

### `document_new`

Create a new RGBA 8-bit sRGB document and make it active. background: colour or 'transparent'.

Parameters: `width`: int = `1024`, `height`: int = `1024`, `name`: str = `'Untitled'`, `background`: str = `'white'`, `resolution_ppi`: float = `72`

### `document_open`

Open a .kra/.ora/.psd or image file from the workspace and make it active.

Parameters: `path`: str

### `document_activate`

Switch the active document (index from krita_status).

Parameters: `index`: int

### `document_info`

Active document details including the full layer tree (listed bottom-to-top) and selection bounds.

### `save_document`

Save the active document as native .kra/.ora in the workspace (omit path to re-save in place).

Parameters: `path`: Optional = `None`

### `export_image`

Export the flattened image to png/jpg/webp/bmp/tiff/psd/ora in the workspace (format from extension).  
layer = export only that layer (cropped to its content unless full_canvas). quality = 0-100 for jpg/webp.  
x/y/width/height = export just that region (e.g. the area to send to an inpainting model).

Parameters: `path`: str, `layer`: Optional = `None`, `quality`: Optional = `None`, `full_canvas`: bool = `False`, `x`: Optional = `None`, `y`: Optional = `None`, `width`: Optional = `None`, `height`: Optional = `None`

### `document_close`

Close the active document. Unsaved changes are discarded unless save=true.

Parameters: `save`: bool = `False`

### `resize_canvas`

Change the canvas size WITHOUT scaling content. Offsets shift existing content.

Parameters: `width`: int, `height`: int, `x_offset`: int = `0`, `y_offset`: int = `0`

### `scale_image`

Scale the whole image (all layers) to a new size. method: Bicubic, Bilinear, Lanczos3, Box,  
Hermite, Mitchell, BSpline or NearestNeighbor (pixel art).

Parameters: `width`: int, `height`: int, `method`: str = `'Bicubic'`

### `crop_image`

Crop the canvas to a rectangle, or to the current selection's bounds when no rectangle is given.

Parameters: `x`: Optional = `None`, `y`: Optional = `None`, `width`: Optional = `None`, `height`: Optional = `None`

### `rotate_image`

Rotate the whole image clockwise by any angle; the canvas grows to fit.

Parameters: `degrees`: float

### `flip`

Mirror the whole image (target=image) or one layer (target=layer). direction: horizontal or vertical.

Parameters: `target`: str = `'image'`, `direction`: str = `'horizontal'`, `layer`: Optional = `None`

### `flatten_image`

Merge all layers into one.

### `convert_color_space`

Convert the image colour space, e.g. depth U16/F16/F32 for high-precision grading, back to RGBA/U8  
for pixel tools. model: RGBA, GRAYA, CMYKA, LABA, XYZA. Profile defaults to sRGB.

Parameters: `model`: str = `'RGBA'`, `depth`: str = `'U8'`, `profile`: Optional = `None`

### `set_guides`

Set the document's guide lines (pixel positions), e.g. thirds or a layout grid the user can see.

Parameters: `horizontal`: Optional = `None`, `vertical`: Optional = `None`, `visible`: Optional = `None`, `clear`: bool = `False`

## Seeing and reading the image

### `canvas_snapshot`

Return the current composite image so you can SEE the canvas. Optionally zoom into a region  
(x, y, width, height in canvas pixels). max_size caps the longest side (64-4096).  
layer = show only that layer (transparent elsewhere).  
grid = draw labelled canvas-coordinate lines every `grid` pixels, to read off exact positions.  
frame = look at another animation frame (the current frame is restored).  
To keep a picture as a file, use export_image (it takes the same region).

Parameters: `max_size`: int = `1024`, `x`: Optional = `None`, `y`: Optional = `None`, `width`: Optional = `None`, `height`: Optional = `None`, `layer`: Optional = `None`, `grid`: Optional = `None`, `frame`: Optional = `None`

### `analyze_image`

Numbers about the image (or a region / one layer): dominant palette with shares, mean colour,  
brightness, contrast, sharpness (0..1), coverage of non-transparent pixels, content bounds, and a  
grid x grid layout of mean colours (top row first). Use it to judge and match colours and lighting.

Parameters: `x`: Optional = `None`, `y`: Optional = `None`, `width`: Optional = `None`, `height`: Optional = `None`, `layer`: Optional = `None`, `palette_size`: int = `8`, `grid`: int = `3`

### `read_pixels`

Exact colours of a small block (max 1024 pixels), rows top to bottom.

Parameters: `x`: int, `y`: int, `width`: int = `8`, `height`: int = `8`, `layer`: Optional = `None`

### `sample_color`

Colour (rgba + '#rrggbbaa') of one pixel of the visible image, or of a single layer if given.

Parameters: `x`: int, `y`: int, `layer`: Optional = `None`

### `find_color`

Where does a colour occur? Returns connected regions (bbox, share, centroid), largest first,  
plus total coverage. Good for locating objects before editing them.

Parameters: `color`: str, `tolerance`: int = `24`, `layer`: Optional = `None`, `x`: Optional = `None`, `y`: Optional = `None`, `width`: Optional = `None`, `height`: Optional = `None`, `limit`: int = `20`

### `view_image`

Look at an image file in the workspace (reference, generated output, export) without importing it.

Parameters: `path`: str, `max_size`: int = `1024`

### `list_workspace`

Files in the workspace folder (path relative to it, size, modified time).

Parameters: `folder`: Optional = `None`, `recursive`: bool = `True`, `limit`: int = `200`

## Layers

### `list_layers`

Layer tree of the active document (children bottom-to-top) and the active layer id.

### `create_layer`

Create a layer or mask; it becomes the active layer. type:  
  paintlayer (fill = optional solid colour), vectorlayer, grouplayer,  
  filllayer (fill = colour, or pattern = pattern resource name) - a non-destructive colour/pattern layer,  
  filterlayer (filter + filter_params) - non-destructive adjustment of everything below,  
  clonelayer (source = layer to mirror live),  
  filelayer (path = image in the workspace, kept as a live link),  
  filllayer with generator = seexpr | screentone | gradient | multigrid and generator_config, e.g.  
    seexpr {"script": "$c = noise(10*$u, 10*$v); [$c, $c*0.8, 1-$c]"} (procedural textures),  
    screentone {"pattern": 0, "shape": 0, "frequency_x": 30, "rotation": 45,  
                "foreground_color": "#000000", "background_color": "#ffffff"} (manga tones),  
    gradient {"shape": "radial", "start_position_x": 50, "start_position_y": 50,  
              "end_position_x": 100, "end_position_y": 50} (uses the user's fg/bg colours),  
  filtermask (filter + filter_params) / transparencymask - attached to `parent` (default: active layer),  
  limited to the current selection if there is one.  
parent = group layer id/name (or the layer a mask attaches to); above = sibling to stack over.

Parameters: `name`: str = `'Layer'`, `type`: str = `'paintlayer'`, `parent`: Optional = `None`, `above`: Optional = `None`, `fill`: Optional = `None`, `filter`: Optional = `None`, `filter_params`: Optional = `None`, `source`: Optional = `None`, `pattern`: Optional = `None`, `path`: Optional = `None`, `generator`: Optional = `None`, `generator_config`: Optional = `None`

### `update_layer`

Change layer properties. layer = id or name (default: active layer). opacity is 0..1.  
blend_mode uses Krita ids such as normal, multiply, screen, overlay, add, color, hue.  
alpha_locked = only paint where the layer already has pixels; clipped = clip to the layers below in the  
group (Krita "inherit alpha"); color_label 0-8.  
x/y place the top-left of the layer's content (its "bounds"); dx/dy move it relative to where it is.

Parameters: `layer`: Optional = `None`, `name`: Optional = `None`, `visible`: Optional = `None`, `opacity`: Optional = `None`, `blend_mode`: Optional = `None`, `locked`: Optional = `None`, `alpha_locked`: Optional = `None`, `clipped`: Optional = `None`, `color_label`: Optional = `None`, `x`: Optional = `None`, `y`: Optional = `None`, `dx`: Optional = `None`, `dy`: Optional = `None`, `activate`: bool = `False`

### `arrange_layer`

Restack a layer. to = top, bottom, up or down; or above = a sibling to sit directly over;  
parent = a group to move the layer into (top of it unless `to`/`above` say otherwise).

Parameters: `layer`: Optional = `None`, `to`: Optional = `None`, `above`: Optional = `None`, `parent`: Optional = `None`

### `merge_down`

Merge a layer (default: active) into the layer below it. Returns the merged layer.

Parameters: `layer`: Optional = `None`

### `delete_layer`

Delete a layer (default: active layer).

Parameters: `layer`: Optional = `None`

### `duplicate_layer`

Duplicate a layer directly above the original.

Parameters: `layer`: Optional = `None`, `name`: Optional = `None`

### `transform_layer`

Scale (about the layer centre), rotate (degrees, clockwise) and/or shear a layer.

Parameters: `layer`: Optional = `None`, `scale_x`: Optional = `None`, `scale_y`: Optional = `None`, `rotate_degrees`: Optional = `None`, `shear_x_degrees`: Optional = `None`, `shear_y_degrees`: Optional = `None`

### `import_image`

Put a raster image on a NEW paint layer. Provide `path` (inside the workspace) OR `image_base64`  
(PNG/JPEG/WebP bytes). fit: contain (default), cover, stretch, none (natural size at x,y), or  
selection (stretched over the selection and masked by it, soft edges included - for inpainting).  
This is how images from an image-generation model get into Krita for further editing.

Parameters: `path`: Optional = `None`, `image_base64`: Optional = `None`, `name`: str = `'Imported image'`, `fit`: Optional = `None`, `x`: Optional = `None`, `y`: Optional = `None`, `width`: Optional = `None`, `height`: Optional = `None`, `parent`: Optional = `None`

### `import_image_from_url`

Download a PUBLIC http(s) image URL (no redirects, max 25 MB, private addresses blocked) and  
place it on a new layer. Same placement options as import_image.

Parameters: `url`: str, `name`: str = `'Imported image'`, `fit`: Optional = `None`, `x`: Optional = `None`, `y`: Optional = `None`, `width`: Optional = `None`, `height`: Optional = `None`

## Painting and drawing

### `brush_stroke`

Paint ONE stroke with Krita's real brush engine (texture, wet mixing, ... from the preset).  
points: [[x, y], ...] or [[x, y, pressure 0..1], ...] (pressure needs a pressure-sensitive preset).  
preset: brush preset name or unique part of it (see list_brush_presets; default: the current brush).  
size in px, opacity/flow 0..1, eraser=true erases with the brush. smooth=true curves through the points.  
closed/fill: close the path / fill it with the colour (outline=false for fill only).  
Painting respects the current selection. The user's own brush settings are restored afterwards.

Parameters: `points`: list, `preset`: Optional = `None`, `size`: Optional = `None`, `color`: Optional = `None`, `opacity`: Optional = `None`, `flow`: Optional = `None`, `eraser`: bool = `False`, `smooth`: bool = `True`, `closed`: bool = `False`, `fill`: bool = `False`, `outline`: bool = `True`, `layer`: Optional = `None`

### `list_brush_presets`

Names of Krita's brush presets (optionally containing `filter`, e.g. 'ink', 'pencil', 'airbrush').

Parameters: `filter`: Optional = `None`, `limit`: int = `200`

### `draw_shapes`

Draw vector-style primitives (anti-aliased) onto a paint layer, in order (max 5000 per call).  
Every shape has "type" and optional "opacity" (0..1). Types:  
  line      {x1,y1,x2,y2,color,stroke_width}  
  polyline  {points:[[x,y],...],color,stroke_width}  
  bezier    {points:[start, c1,c2,end, c1,c2,end ...],color,stroke_width}   (1+3n points)  
  rect      {x,y,width,height,radius?,fill?,stroke?,stroke_width?,gradient?}  
  ellipse   {cx,cy,rx,ry,fill?,stroke?,stroke_width?,gradient?}  
  polygon   {points:[[x,y],...],fill?,stroke?,stroke_width?,gradient?}  
  text      {x,y,text,size(px),font?,bold?,color}   (x,y = baseline-left)  
For closed shapes `color` is the fill when neither fill nor stroke is given.  
gradient: {"type":"linear","x1","y1","x2","y2","stops":[[0,"#fff"],[1,"#000"]]} or  
          {"type":"radial","cx","cy","r","stops":[...]}.  
layer = id or name of a paint layer (default: active layer).  
These are crisp geometric shapes; for painterly marks use brush_stroke.

Parameters: `shapes`: list, `layer`: Optional = `None`

### `add_svg`

Add SVG elements as EDITABLE vector shapes: <path>, <rect>, <circle>, <ellipse>, <polygon>, <line>,  
<text>, gradients in <defs>, groups. Bare elements use canvas pixel coordinates. Goes onto `layer`  
(a vectorlayer), the active vector layer, or a new vector layer called `name`.  
No external references (href/url() only to #ids, images as data: URIs).

Parameters: `svg`: str, `layer`: Optional = `None`, `name`: str = `'Vector'`

### `list_vector_shapes`

Shapes on a vector layer: name, type, bbox in pixels (optionally each shape's SVG).

Parameters: `layer`: Optional = `None`, `include_svg`: bool = `False`

### `remove_vector_shapes`

Delete shapes by name from a vector layer (["all"] removes every shape).

Parameters: `names`: list, `layer`: Optional = `None`

### `colorize_lineart`

Flat-colour line art with Krita's Colourise Mask: regions = [{"color": "#e0b090",  
"points": [[x,y],...] (a scribble inside the area)} or {"color": ..., "rect": [x,y,w,h]}].  
Krita floods each scribble's colour up to the lines. transparent_color marks areas to leave empty.

Parameters: `regions`: list, `layer`: Optional = `None`, `transparent_color`: Optional = `None`, `edge_detection`: bool = `False`, `cleanup`: float = `0.7`, `name`: str = `'Colourise'`

## Game art and pixel art

### `ink_stroke`

Variable-width ink: line art, lettering, calligraphy. Thick where pressure is high, thin at tapered ends  
(unlike draw_shapes' even lines), and crisp and exact (unlike brush_stroke's textured brushes).  
points: [[x, y], ...] or [[x, y, pressure 0..1], ...] for one stroke; strokes: [{points, width?, color?,  
opacity?, taper_start?, taper_end?, ...}, ...] for many at once (max 20000 points per call).  
width = the widest width in px; taper_start/taper_end = how much of the length thins out (0..1);  
smoothing 0..5 rounds the corners between points; min_width keeps the ends from vanishing.

Parameters: `points`: Optional = `None`, `strokes`: Optional = `None`, `width`: float = `8`, `color`: str = `'#000000'`, `opacity`: float = `1.0`, `taper_start`: float = `0.2`, `taper_end`: float = `0.35`, `smoothing`: int = `2`, `min_width`: float = `0`, `layer`: Optional = `None`, `antialias`: bool = `True`

### `outline_layer`

An outline around what is on a layer - a sprite, a sticker, text. width 1..64 px.  
position: outside (on a new layer below; the classic sprite/sticker outline) or inside the edge (above).  
shape: round, square (thick corners) or diamond (width 1 = the pixel-art outline without corners).  
threshold = the alpha (1..255) a pixel needs to count as solid. new_layer=false paints into the layer.

Parameters: `layer`: Optional = `None`, `width`: int = `1`, `color`: str = `'#000000'`, `position`: str = `'outside'`, `shape`: str = `'round'`, `threshold`: int = `128`, `new_layer`: bool = `True`, `name`: Optional = `None`

### `quantize_layer`

Repaint a layer with a limited palette - pixel art, retro and print looks, consistent game sprites.  
palette = the colours to use (e.g. a console's palette, or layer_colors of another sprite); otherwise the  
best `colors` (2..256) found in the layer. dither: none (flat), ordered (retro pattern) or floyd (smooth).  
strength = how strong the ordered pattern is. alpha_threshold = make every pixel fully opaque or fully  
transparent (crisp sprite edges). Works inside the selection if there is one. Returns the palette used.

Parameters: `layer`: Optional = `None`, `colors`: int = `16`, `palette`: Optional = `None`, `dither`: str = `'none'`, `strength`: float = `48`, `alpha_threshold`: Optional = `None`, `ignore_selection`: bool = `False`

### `swap_colors`

Palette swap: [["#ff0000", "#0000ff"], ...] replaces each first colour with the second - recolour a  
sprite, make team colours or variants. tolerance 0..255 also catches near colours (anti-aliased edges).  
Each pixel keeps its own transparency. Works inside the selection if there is one.

Parameters: `pairs`: list, `layer`: Optional = `None`, `tolerance`: int = `0`, `ignore_selection`: bool = `False`

### `layer_colors`

The colours a layer uses: every one when there are at most max_colors (pixel art: exact = true), else its  
main ones. Use it as a palette for quantize_layer or to plan a swap_colors.

Parameters: `layer`: Optional = `None`, `max_colors`: int = `64`

### `export_layers`

Save each layer as its own PNG in a workspace folder, cropped to what is on it (trim), plus manifest.json  
with each layer's file, position (x, y), size, stacking order (z, 0 = bottom), opacity and blend mode - what a  
game engine, an animation tool or a web page needs to rebuild the picture. layers = only these (ids, names  
or "Group/Layer" paths); merge_groups = one picture per group; include_hidden = hidden layers too.

Parameters: `folder`: str = `'layers'`, `layers`: Optional = `None`, `trim`: bool = `True`, `merge_groups`: bool = `False`, `include_hidden`: bool = `False`

### `slice_sheet`

Cut a sprite sheet or tileset into tiles, each saved as a PNG in a workspace folder, with <prefix>.json  
listing every tile's file, row, column and position. Give tile_width/tile_height (px), or columns/rows.  
margin = border around the sheet, spacing = gap between tiles. layer = slice only that layer (default: the  
whole picture). skip_empty leaves out fully transparent tiles.

Parameters: `tile_width`: Optional = `None`, `tile_height`: Optional = `None`, `columns`: Optional = `None`, `rows`: Optional = `None`, `margin`: int = `0`, `spacing`: int = `0`, `layer`: Optional = `None`, `folder`: str = `'tiles'`, `prefix`: str = `'tile'`, `skip_empty`: bool = `True`

## Generative AI

### `ai_backends`

Which generative-AI services are connected: image backends (ComfyUI, AUTOMATIC1111/Forge, OpenAI,  
Gemini, Stability, Replicate, fal) with their models/samplers/upscalers, video backends (HeyGen, Sora,  
Veo, Replicate, fal; details=true lists HeyGen avatars and voices), vision models for ask_vision, and  
the ComfyUI workflows saved in <workspace>/workflows. Call this before generate_image.

Parameters: `details`: bool = `False`

### `generate_image`

Generate pixels with an image model and place them as NEW layers (one undo step).  
mode: auto (inpaint if there is a selection, else txt2img), txt2img, img2img (rework the region;  
strength 0..1 = how much changes), inpaint (regenerate only the selected pixels; soft edges blend).  
The region is the selection's bounds + padding (or x/y/width/height, or region='canvas'); results are  
cut to the selection, so nothing outside it changes. count 1-8 = variations in a group plus a numbered  
comparison sheet (choose with pick_variation). backend: comfyui, a1111, openai, gemini, stability,  
replicate, fal (default: KRITAPILOT_IMAGE_BACKEND or the first available - see ai_backends).  
model = checkpoint / model id (Replicate 'owner/name', fal 'fal-ai/...'). size = longest side to  
generate at (default 1024). workflow = a ComfyUI API-format graph saved as <workspace>/workflows/NAME.json  
using {{prompt}} {{negative}} {{seed}} {{image}} {{mask}} {{width}} {{height}} {{strength}} placeholders  
(ControlNet, IP-Adapter, Flux, ... anything ComfyUI can do). extra = provider-specific inputs.  
control = guide the composition with a layer, e.g. [{"layer": "Sketch", "type": "lineart",  
"strength": 0.8}] - paint a sketch / pose / depth layer and the model follows it. type: lineart, scribble,  
canny, softedge, depth, openpose, normal, seg, tile, ...; model = ControlNet model (default: the first  
installed whose name contains the type); preprocess = A1111 preprocessor (e.g. depth_midas when the layer  
is a photo); start/end 0..1; layer omitted = the whole picture. Real ControlNet on comfyui / a1111  
(several guides at once; in workflows use {{control}} / {{control_1}}...); stability uses its sketch /  
structure control; openai and gemini receive the guide as the image to follow.  
style = a look recipe added to the prompt (with a matching negative prompt): photo, cinematic, portrait,  
product, fashion, street, landscape, macro, food, architecture, drone (realistic) or concept_art,  
illustration, anime, watercolor, oil_painting, 3d_render, pixel_art, comic, sketch.

Parameters: `prompt`: str, `mode`: str = `'auto'`, `negative_prompt`: Optional = `None`, `count`: int = `1`, `backend`: Optional = `None`, `model`: Optional = `None`, `strength`: Optional = `None`, `seed`: Optional = `None`, `steps`: Optional = `None`, `cfg`: Optional = `None`, `sampler`: Optional = `None`, `scheduler`: Optional = `None`, `size`: Optional = `None`, `workflow`: Optional = `None`, `region`: str = `'auto'`, `x`: Optional = `None`, `y`: Optional = `None`, `width`: Optional = `None`, `height`: Optional = `None`, `padding`: int = `32`, `name`: Optional = `None`, `extra`: Optional = `None`, `control`: Optional = `None`, `style`: Optional = `None`

### `edit_image`

Change the picture by describing the change, like a photo editor that understands words: "make it  
night", "remove the person on the left", "turn it into a watercolour", "add snow on the roofs", "make her  
smile". With a selection only that area changes (select it first, e.g. with select_by_description);  
otherwise the whole picture. The result is a NEW layer above, so the original stays untouched.  
Uses image models that edit by instruction first - Gemini, OpenAI (gpt-image), Flux Kontext on fal or  
Replicate - then any other connected service (img2img; `strength` 0..1 = how much changes).

Parameters: `instruction`: str, `backend`: Optional = `None`, `model`: Optional = `None`, `strength`: Optional = `None`, `region`: str = `'auto'`, `name`: Optional = `None`

### `pick_variation`

Show variant `index` (1-based, as numbered on the sheet) of a generate_image variants group.  
keep_only=true deletes the other variants and leaves just the chosen layer.

Parameters: `group`: str, `index`: int = `1`, `keep_only`: bool = `False`

### `generation_history`

The pictures image models made recently, newest first: id, time, prompt, service, model and how many  
pictures. Bring one back with place_generation(id), or reuse its prompt.

Parameters: `limit`: int = `10`

### `place_generation`

Put a picture from generation_history back on the canvas, as a new layer covering the picture  
(index = which of its variations, from 1).

Parameters: `id`: str, `index`: int = `1`, `name`: Optional = `None`

### `outpaint`

Extend the picture beyond its edges: grows the canvas by left/right/top/bottom pixels, selects the  
new border (reaching `overlap` px into the old image so it blends) and inpaints it.

Parameters: `prompt`: str, `left`: int = `0`, `right`: int = `0`, `top`: int = `0`, `bottom`: int = `0`, `overlap`: int = `24`, `negative_prompt`: Optional = `None`, `count`: int = `1`, `backend`: Optional = `None`, `model`: Optional = `None`, `seed`: Optional = `None`, `size`: Optional = `None`, `workflow`: Optional = `None`

### `upscale_image`

AI super-resolution: scales the document by `factor` (all layers, Lanczos) and adds the model's  
upscaled rendering of the whole picture as a new top layer. backend: a1111 / comfyui (their upscale  
models), stability, replicate, fal. Without an AI backend use scale_image.

Parameters: `factor`: float = `2.0`, `backend`: Optional = `None`, `model`: Optional = `None`

### `remove_background`

Cut the subject out of a layer. mode: mask (non-destructive transparency mask, default), erase, or  
select (just select the subject). method: color (local, no AI: floods the plain background in from the  
image border, within `tolerance` of the border colour or of `color`), ai (a segmentation model via  
stability / replicate / fal / a1111 with the rembg extension), auto (ai if a capable backend answers,  
else color).

Parameters: `layer`: Optional = `None`, `method`: str = `'auto'`, `mode`: str = `'mask'`, `tolerance`: int = `32`, `feather`: int = `1`, `color`: Optional = `None`, `backend`: Optional = `None`, `model`: Optional = `None`

### `match_colors`

Make a layer's colours sit in the scene: transfers the mean and contrast of each channel from a  
reference (another layer, an image file in the workspace, or a region [x,y,w,h] of the picture - by  
default the whole picture). Use after pasting or generating an element. Respects the selection.

Parameters: `layer`: Optional = `None`, `reference_layer`: Optional = `None`, `reference_path`: Optional = `None`, `reference_region`: Optional = `None`, `strength`: float = `1.0`

### `generate_video`

Make a video with a video model, save it in the workspace and (by default) open it in Krita as an  
animation to paint over, grade or re-render. use_canvas=true sends the current picture as the start  
frame (image-to-video) or, for HeyGen, as the background behind the avatar.  
backend: heygen (talking avatar: script + avatar_id + voice_id; character='photo' makes the character  
painted on the canvas talk), openai (Sora), gemini (Veo), replicate / fal (any video model id).  
camera = a cinematic camera move written into the prompt: dolly_in, dolly_out, push_in, pull_back,  
crash_zoom, pan_left/right, tilt_up/down, orbit_left/right, crane_up/down, handheld, fpv_drone, whip_pan,  
bullet_time, ken_burns, static. style = a look (cinematic, photo, anime, ... as in generate_image).  
Generation can take several minutes. (No video model? camera_move animates the picture locally.)  
Side effects: sends the prompt (and, with use_canvas, the current picture) to the chosen cloud service, WRITES  
the video file into the workspace (path, or an automatic name; an existing file of that name is replaced) and  
by default opens it in Krita as a new document/animated layer.

Parameters: `prompt`: str = `''`, `backend`: Optional = `None`, `model`: Optional = `None`, `use_canvas`: bool = `True`, `seconds`: Optional = `None`, `width`: Optional = `None`, `height`: Optional = `None`, `script`: Optional = `None`, `avatar_id`: Optional = `None`, `voice_id`: Optional = `None`, `character`: str = `'avatar'`, `negative_prompt`: Optional = `None`, `path`: Optional = `None`, `import_into_krita`: bool = `True`, `max_frames`: int = `240`, `extra`: Optional = `None`, `camera`: Optional = `None`, `style`: Optional = `None`

### `ask_vision`

Ask another vision AI about the canvas and get its answer as text: a second opinion or critique,  
a caption, or a detailed prompt for an image model. provider: anthropic (Claude), openai (GPT, or any  
OpenAI-compatible server such as Ollama or LM Studio), gemini. Optionally a region or a single layer.

Parameters: `question`: str, `provider`: Optional = `None`, `model`: Optional = `None`, `max_size`: int = `1024`, `x`: Optional = `None`, `y`: Optional = `None`, `width`: Optional = `None`, `height`: Optional = `None`, `layer`: Optional = `None`

## Asset libraries

### `search_assets`

Find free real-world material to make work realistic. kind:  
textures - Poly Haven CC0 photo textures (rock, wood, bark, fabric, leather, skin, metal, ground, ...),  
hdris    - Poly Haven CC0 HDRI panoramas as photographic skies and backdrops,  
photos   - Openverse openly licensed photos for reference or compositing (licence: e.g. 'cc0,pdm' for no  
           attribution, or 'by,by-sa'); results include the attribution text.  
Then import_asset(id, kind).

Parameters: `query`: str = `''`, `kind`: str = `'textures'`, `limit`: int = `12`, `licence`: Optional = `None`

### `import_asset`

Put a search_assets result on a new layer. Textures tile across the canvas by default (tile_size = px per  
tile; texture_map: diffuse, normal, roughness, ao, displacement); hdris and photos cover the canvas  
(fit: cover, contain, stretch, tile, none). To texture a painted shape: import it, then  
update_layer(clipped=true, blend_mode='overlay' or 'multiply') above the shape in the same group.  
Returns the layer and the attribution to credit (photos).

Parameters: `id`: str, `kind`: str = `'textures'`, `resolution`: str = `'2k'`, `texture_map`: str = `'diffuse'`, `fit`: Optional = `None`, `tile_size`: Optional = `None`, `name`: Optional = `None`, `blend_mode`: Optional = `None`, `opacity`: Optional = `None`, `parent`: Optional = `None`

## Photo editing

### `adjust_image`

Photo adjustment on a paint layer (limited to the selection if any). operation + settings:  
exact tone tools (pixel-precise, channel = rgb|r|g|b):  
  levels {in_black, in_white, gamma, out_black, out_white} · curves {points: [[in,out],...] 0-255}  
  brightness_contrast {brightness, contrast -100..100} · exposure {stops} · gamma {gamma}  
  temperature {temperature -100..100 (warm+), tint -100..100 (magenta+)}  
Krita filters (non_destructive=true adds them as an editable filter mask instead):  
  hue_saturation {hue -180..180, saturation, lightness -100..100, colorize}  
  color_balance {shadows_|midtones_|highlights_ + cyan_red|magenta_green|yellow_blue: -100..100}  
  sharpen {amount 0-10, radius, threshold} · blur {radius} · motion_blur {angle, length}  
  lens_blur {radius} · denoise {strength} · denoise_gaussian {threshold, window}  
  desaturate {method} · auto_contrast · normalize · invert · posterize {steps}  
  threshold {level} · pixelize {size} · oil_paint {brush_size, smooth} · emboss {depth}  
  edge_detect {radius} · high_pass {radius} · noise {amount, opacity, grayscale}  
  color_to_alpha {color, threshold} · dodge / burn {exposure 0-1, range 0 shadows|1 mid|2 highlights}  
  wave {amplitude, wavelength} · round_corners {radius}  
Any other Krita filter: apply_filter.

Parameters: `operation`: str, `settings`: Optional = `None`, `layer`: Optional = `None`, `non_destructive`: bool = `False`

### `auto_enhance`

One-click photo fix: stretch the tonal range (per channel also removes colour casts).

Parameters: `layer`: Optional = `None`, `clip_percent`: float = `0.5`, `per_channel`: bool = `True`

### `add_vignette`

Darken (or tint) the edges on a new layer on top; adjust its opacity or delete it later.

Parameters: `strength`: float = `0.5`, `size`: float = `0.65`, `color`: str = `'#000000'`, `blend_mode`: str = `'normal'`

### `apply_filter`

Apply a Krita filter (blur, levels, invert, ...) to a paint layer, restricted to the selection if any.  
params: filter properties from describe_filter (string/number/bool values only).

Parameters: `name`: str, `params`: Optional = `None`, `layer`: Optional = `None`, `ignore_selection`: bool = `False`

### `list_filters`

Names of all Krita filters usable with apply_filter.

### `describe_filter`

Default parameters of a filter, so you know which `params` apply_filter accepts.

Parameters: `name`: str

## Selections

### `set_selection`

Select: kind=rect or ellipse (x, y, width, height), polygon (points [[x,y],...]),  
layer (the opaque pixels of `layer`), color (every pixel within `tolerance` 0-255 of `color`, or of the  
colour at x,y; contiguous=true = magic wand from x,y), all, or none.  
mode: replace, add, subtract, intersect. Later draw/brush/filter/fill operations are limited to it.

Parameters: `kind`: str = `'rect'`, `x`: Optional = `None`, `y`: Optional = `None`, `width`: Optional = `None`, `height`: Optional = `None`, `points`: Optional = `None`, `layer`: Optional = `None`, `color`: Optional = `None`, `tolerance`: Optional = `None`, `contiguous`: bool = `False`, `mode`: str = `'replace'`

### `select_by_description`

Select something by describing it: "the sky", "the person on the left", "all the windows", "the red  
car". Makes a real Krita selection you can then edit, mask, fill or pass to edit_image / generate_image.  
mode: replace, add, subtract, intersect (with the current selection). method: auto (best available),  
gemini (pixel-accurate masks; needs a Gemini key), fal (a segmentation model; needs a fal key), or vision  
(any vision chat model outlines it - free with Pollinations, but approximate). layer = look at one layer  
only. feather = soft edge in pixels.

Parameters: `what`: str, `mode`: str = `'replace'`, `method`: str = `'auto'`, `layer`: Optional = `None`, `feather`: int = `1`, `provider`: Optional = `None`, `model`: Optional = `None`

### `modify_selection`

operation: invert, grow, shrink, feather, border or smooth. amount in pixels.

Parameters: `operation`: str, `amount`: int = `1`

### `fill_selection`

Fill the current selection on a paint layer with a colour; omit colour to erase the selected pixels.

Parameters: `color`: Optional = `None`, `layer`: Optional = `None`

### `export_selection_mask`

Save the current selection as a greyscale PNG mask (white = selected) for inpainting models.

Parameters: `path`: str, `invert`: bool = `False`

## Animation and video

### `animation_info`

Frame rate, playback/clip range, current frame and animated layers.

### `animation_set`

Set frame rate, frame range (start..end) and/or go to `frame` (drawing then edits that frame).

Parameters: `fps`: Optional = `None`, `start`: Optional = `None`, `end`: Optional = `None`, `frame`: Optional = `None`

### `keyframe`

Keyframe operation on a paint layer at `frame`: blank (new empty drawing), duplicate (copy of the  
previous drawing), remove, remove_and_pull (shift later frames back), hold (insert a hold frame,  
shifting later ones), unhold. The layer becomes animated; draw on it while at that frame.

Parameters: `frame`: int, `kind`: str = `'blank'`, `layer`: Optional = `None`

### `list_keyframes`

Frames at which a layer has keyframes.

Parameters: `layer`: Optional = `None`, `start`: Optional = `None`, `end`: Optional = `None`

### `import_frames`

Load image files from the workspace (in order) as frames of a new animated layer.

Parameters: `paths`: list, `first_frame`: int = `0`, `step`: int = `1`

### `animation_contact_sheet`

See many frames at once: a labelled grid of frames (max 48) to review motion and consistency.

Parameters: `start`: Optional = `None`, `end`: Optional = `None`, `step`: Optional = `None`, `columns`: Optional = `None`, `cell_size`: int = `256`

### `export_animation_frames`

Render frames as numbered PNGs into a workspace folder.

Parameters: `folder`: str = `'frames'`, `start`: Optional = `None`, `end`: Optional = `None`, `prefix`: str = `'frame'`

### `video_info`

Size, fps, duration, frame count, codec and audio presence of a video in the workspace.

Parameters: `path`: str

### `import_video`

Decode a video (mp4/mov/webm/mkv/avi/gif...) from the workspace into an animated layer so every  
frame can be painted, filtered or adjusted. Opens a new document sized to the video unless  
into_current. start/duration in seconds; fps resamples; width scales (keeps aspect). Max 1000 frames.

Parameters: `path`: str, `start`: float = `0`, `duration`: Optional = `None`, `fps`: Optional = `None`, `max_frames`: int = `240`, `width`: Optional = `None`, `into_current`: bool = `False`, `name`: Optional = `None`

### `render_video`

Render the animation (default: playback range) to .mp4 (H.264), .webm (VP9), .gif, .mov (ProRes),  
.mkv or .apng in the workspace, using the ffmpeg bundled with Krita. width scales the output.

Parameters: `path`: str, `start`: Optional = `None`, `end`: Optional = `None`, `fps`: Optional = `None`, `width`: Optional = `None`, `quality`: Optional = `None`, `bitrate_kbps`: Optional = `None`

### `camera_move`

Bring a still to life without any AI model: renders the current picture through a moving virtual camera  
into an animation (a new document by default). move: dolly_in, dolly_out, push_in, pull_back, zoom_in,  
zoom_out, crash_zoom, pan_left, pan_right, tilt_up, tilt_down, orbit_left, orbit_right, crane_up,  
crane_down, handheld, ken_burns, static. intensity 0.1-3. render_path = also render it, e.g. 'shot.mp4'.

Parameters: `move`: str = `'dolly_in'`, `seconds`: float = `3.0`, `fps`: int = `24`, `intensity`: float = `1.0`, `width`: Optional = `None`, `new_document`: bool = `True`, `render_path`: Optional = `None`

### `for_each_frame`

Apply the same tool calls to every frame of an animation / imported video, e.g. colour-grade a clip:  
[{"tool": "adjust_image", "args": {"operation": "temperature", "settings": {"temperature": 30}}}].  
Frames default to the playback range (max 1000 frames, 20 operations).

Parameters: `operations`: list, `start`: Optional = `None`, `end`: Optional = `None`, `step`: int = `1`

## Controls

### `krita_action`

Run one of Krita's own commands on the active document/layer (curated, no dialogs):  
selection: select_all, deselect, reselect, invert_selection, select_opaque(_add|_subtract|_intersect),  
  copy_selection_to_new_layer, cut_selection_to_new_layer, clear_selection_pixels,  
  fill_with_foreground, fill_with_background, fill_with_pattern, selection_to_vector_shape  
layers: convert_to_paint_layer, convert_to_animated_layer, convert_group_to_animated,  
  convert_to_transparency_mask, convert_to_selection_mask, alpha_into_mask, flatten_layer,  
  isolate_layer, isolate_group, rotate_layer_90_cw|90_ccw|180, mirror_all_layers_horizontally|vertically  
image: rotate_image_90_cw|90_ccw|180, trim_to_image, trim_to_layer, trim_to_selection,  
  duplicate_image_as_new_document, create_snapshot  
animation: next_frame, previous_frame, next_keyframe, previous_keyframe, first_frame, last_frame,  
  toggle_onion_skin, play_pause, stop_playback  
view: zoom_to_fit, zoom_to_100, zoom_in, zoom_out, mirror_view, rotate_view_left|right, reset_view,  
  toggle_wrap_around, toggle_grid, toggle_pixel_grid, toggle_guides, toggle_rulers,  
  toggle_selection_display, toggle_canvas_only

Parameters: `name`: str, `layer`: Optional = `None`

### `view_control`

Move the user's view of the canvas (not the image): zoom (1.0 = 100%), rotation in degrees,  
mirror, fit to window, reset, or centre on a canvas point - e.g. to show the user what you changed.

Parameters: `zoom`: Optional = `None`, `rotation`: Optional = `None`, `mirror`: Optional = `None`, `fit`: bool = `False`, `reset`: bool = `False`, `center_x`: Optional = `None`, `center_y`: Optional = `None`

### `notify_user`

Show a short floating message on the user's Krita canvas.

Parameters: `message`: str, `seconds`: int = `4`

### `user_tool_state`

Read (no arguments) or set the colours and brush the USER paints with next - e.g. hand them the  
palette colour or brush you used. Returns the current state.

Parameters: `foreground`: Optional = `None`, `background`: Optional = `None`, `preset`: Optional = `None`, `size`: Optional = `None`, `opacity`: Optional = `None`, `flow`: Optional = `None`, `blend_mode`: Optional = `None`, `eraser`: Optional = `None`

## Resources

### `list_resources`

Names of Krita resources: type = preset (brushes), pattern, gradient, palette, brush, workspace.

Parameters: `type`: str = `'preset'`, `filter`: Optional = `None`, `limit`: int = `200`

### `palette_colors`

The colours (name + hex) of a Krita palette resource, for a coherent colour scheme.

Parameters: `name`: str

## History and batching

### `undo`

Undo your last edit(s) (each tool call is one step: pixels, layer changes, selection...).  
native=true steps through Krita's own undo stack instead (also covers edits made by hand).

Parameters: `steps`: int = `1`, `native`: bool = `False`

### `redo`

Redo edit(s) undone with undo.

Parameters: `steps`: int = `1`, `native`: bool = `False`

### `history`

Your undoable edits in the active document plus Krita's own undo stack (done=false = undone).

Parameters: `limit`: int = `30`

### `batch`

Run several tool calls in one go, in order: [{"tool": "draw_shapes", "args": {...}}, ...] (max 200).  
Any tool except batch itself. Returns one result per operation; images (canvas_snapshot,  
view_image) are returned after the summary. Much faster than one call per step.  
operations_file = read the operations from a .json file in the workspace instead (a list, or  
{"operations": [...]}) - for long stroke lists that are too big to send in one message.

Parameters: `operations`: Optional = `None`, `stop_on_error`: bool = `True`, `operations_file`: Optional = `None`

## Other

### `find_skills`

Find skills - step-by-step know-how for kinds of Krita work (photoreal images, hand painting,  
retouching, video, and any the user installed). Search with a few words about the task; then load the  
one that fits with use_skill. Cheap: returns names and one-line descriptions only.

Parameters: `query`: str = `''`, `limit`: int = `8`

### `use_skill`

Load a skill's instructions (from find_skills) and follow them. file = one of the extra text files the  
skill lists (references, templates). Skills are text only; nothing in them is executed.

Parameters: `name`: str, `file`: Optional = `None`

## Prompts

Ready-made workflows that MCP clients offer as slash commands or templates:

- **`create`** (`request`) - Make anything from a prompt: Krita decides whether to generate it (realistic) or paint it.
- **`paint_scene`** (`subject`, `style` (optional)) - Plan and paint a scene with Krita's own tools, then critique and refine it.
- **`generative_inpaint`** (`change`) - Change part of the picture with an image model while keeping everything else.
- **`concept_variations`** (`brief`, `count` (optional)) - Explore several design directions quickly, then develop the best.
- **`retouch_photo`** (`goal` (optional)) - Retouch the open photo: tone, colour, cleanup, finish.
- **`animate`** (`idea`, `frames` (optional)) - Make a short frame-by-frame or AI-assisted animation.
- **`product_shot`** (`product`, `setting` (optional)) - Cut out a product and stage it in a newly generated setting.
